Reason.description: One reason, or one recorded WARN line.

Refusal.description: Why a run's results were refused.

reasons.description:
The verdict's reasons, for a run that failed or was cancelled; the output signals' reasons
judged now, for `results_outputs_invalid`; otherwise empty.

refusal.description: What `simpa results <run> --json` prints when it refuses a run.

exit_code.description: The CLI's exit code: 5 for a failed or cancelled run, 6 for results that do not verify.

refusal.title: RefusalReport

AggregateReport.description:
All bands of a receiver summed bin by bin (`params::aggregate`): **an aggregate, not a band,
and not ISO 3382-1's single-number value** (the arithmetic mean of band values), since its
decay is weighted by the source spectrum.

aggregate.description: [`AGGREGATE_BANDS_SUMMED`] for SPPS; [`AGGREGATE_NO_SERIES`] for a TCR receiver.

bands_hz.description: The bands summed: those whose series `params` accepts. Empty for TCR.

crossings_per_particle.description:
As for a band: the aggregate's own (its bands' particles together, counted at the least
deposit of any band, with the largest lifetime spread of any); `null` for TCR.

AnalyticBandReport.description: `core::params`' Sabine and Eyring times for one band, on the run's inputs.

air_m_per_metre.description: The energy attenuation TCR adds as `4·m·V`, 1/m; `null` with air absorption off.

AnalyticReport.description: The analytic references on the run's own inputs (`tcr::analytic`), or why there are none.

Arrival.description: When the direct sound arrived, which every onset-relative quantity is measured from.

oneOf.description:
Not given: somewhere in the onset bin. Each quantity is computed with the arrival at both
ends of the bin, and refused as `unresolved` when the two differ by more than its limit.

Given, such as the source–receiver distance over the speed of sound. For C50, C80, D50 and
Ts it must lie in the onset bin; otherwise those four are refused, `params_bad_arrival`.
The decay times are computed whatever the arrival ([`evaluate`]).

half_width_s.description:
The direct sound reaches the receiver over `[time_s − half_width_s, time_s +
half_width_s]`, not at one instant: a ball of radius `R` crossed at `c` takes `2R/c`
(`docs/params.md`, "The direct sound's spread"). 0 for an impulse.

BandEnergy.description: One band's series of a whole-room table (`<cumul_filename>`).

BandStats.description: One band's column. The field order is the row order.

freq_hz.description: The band, from the column label `<f> Hz`.

CurvatureReport.description:
The curvature of a decay (`params::decay::curvature`), for M8 and M12 to decide what a curved
decay may show: its value with its Monte-Carlo standard deviation, and the flag.

curved.description:
`|percent| > limit_percent`: a curved (double-slope) decay. `null` when `percent` is
refused.

percent.description:
`100·(T30/T20 − 1)`, %, from the reported T20 and T30, with its standard deviation over
the Monte-Carlo resamples; refused, with T30's refusal or else T20's, when either is.

DecayCurve.description:
The Schroeder curve EDT, T20 and T30 are fitted to, for display (`docs/formats/results-json.md`,
"The decay curve"): the same curve, from the same code, not a second computation of it.

from_s.description:
The time, s, of the curve's `u = 0`: the arrival the decay times are measured from
([`BandParameters::decay_arrival`]); with the arrival detected, the start of the onset bin,
the first of the two ends the decay times are read from.

histogram_from_s.description:
From this `u` on, every knot is the histogram's own backward sum at a bin edge. Before it
the curve is the model's reading: the direct sound a step at `u = 0`, then the decay of the
first bin wholly after the direct sound continued back to the arrival
(`docs/params.md`, "The curve between bin edges"). When the series' early reverberation is
unresolved, the values are read two more ways over this stretch
([`EnergySeries::with_early_reverberation_unresolved`]); the curve shown is this reading.

knots.description: The knots of the whole curve, before any is left out.

points.description:
`[u, level]`: `u` in s since `from_s`, the level in dB re the curve's value at `u = 0`,
which includes the direct sound. Joined by straight lines they are the curve within
`tolerance_db`: the curve is straight in dB between its knots, and a knot is left out only
when the line through the points kept either side of it passes within `tolerance_db` of it
and of every other knot left out between them. The first point is `[0, 0]`; the second,
also at `u = 0`, is the level just after the direct sound (the curve steps down by it at
the arrival). The last is the start of the last bin with energy: inside that bin the curve
falls to nothing, which a level cannot show, and the fits leave it out.

Entry.description:
One quantity's calibration under one method (and, for energetic T20 and T30, one kind of
band).

factor.description:
`k`: the largest one-sided 95 % upper bound, over the calibration cells, of the ratio of
the seeds' spread to `√(1 + kappa·n)` times the bootstrap, rounded up to two digits
(rule R3-1).

kappa.description: `κ`: how much a particle's crossings of one receiver at several times add (R3-1).

margin.description:
A refusal names the particle count at which the calibrated standard deviation would be
the limit over this margin: one run's own estimate scatters from seed to seed, so a
count named from one run can fall short (rule 5b over round 3's calibration cells).

max_crossings_per_particle.description:
... and the most crossings per particle, `n`. Outside it the value is refused,
`noise_uncalibrated`.

min_particles.description: The domain (R3-5): the fewest particles per source the quantity was calibrated at ...

resampled_confirmed.description:
Whether a value its resamples refuse names the count at which they would not (R4-3):
false where such counts were not borne out at a pair's higher count (round 4, F8).

root_n_confirmed.description:
Whether a refusal names a count: the seeds' spread did not fall slower than `1/√N` on
any pair of cells that differ only in `N` (rule R3-6, one-sided).

structure.description: How the resamples the factor applies to are drawn ([`super::Structure`]).

anyOf.description: In the quantity's unit (the field name says it).

Evaluated.description: A quantity's value, or why it has none.

FreePathSettings.description:
The settings the transport traced with: its own, nothing of any solver. [`free_paths`] always
uses [`FreePathSettings::STANDARD`] and takes no settings from its caller; others are for
studies of the transport in test builds.

burn_in_paths.description:
Free paths of each ray left out after its first (from its start to a face, never
counted), while the ray forgets where it started.

paths_per_ray.description: Free paths counted per ray after the burn-in. At least 2.

rays_per_replica.description:
Rays per replica, each started at a point drawn evenly from the enclosure's volume, in an
isotropic direction.

replicas.description:
Independent replicas, each its own random stream, traced on as many threads as the
machine has. At least 2. The statistical errors are over the rays, each ray's paths summed
first.

seed.description:
The seed of the replicas' random streams. In JSON, `0x` and 16 hex digits: a number above
2⁵³ would not survive a reader that parses numbers as doubles.

FreePaths.description: The free paths between reflections of a diffuse (Lambert) ray transport in the room, computed from its geometry alone at fixed settings (params::lambert::free_paths): their mean and relative variance gamma^2, with their standard errors over the transport's rays, and the room's 4V/S, V and S.

four_v_over_s_m.description: Kosten's `4V/S`, m, which the mean free path was checked against.

gamma2_se.description: Its standard error over the rays (the delta method's).

mean_free_path_se_m.description: Its standard error over the rays, m.

Method.description:
SPPS's computation method (`computation_method`): how a crossing's deposit is modelled, and
which of [`calibration`]'s tables apply.

oneOf.description: Code 0: a particle keeps its start energy until it is absorbed whole.
Code 1: a particle's energy falls at every reflection.

MonteCarloReport.description: How every SPPS value's Monte-Carlo noise was estimated and judged (`params::noise`).

calibration.description:
Per quantity, by name, for this computation method (`params::noise::calibration`;
`docs/investigations/2026-09-25-noise-calibration/`): each value's standard deviation is
the bootstrap's times `factor·√(1 + kappa·n)`, and a value is given only with at least
`min_particles` particles per source and `n` at most `max_crossings_per_particle`.

crossings_variable.description:
What `n`, the crossings of a receiver per particle each band's `crossings_per_particle`
gives, is for this method (`params::noise::calibration::variable`).

limit_decay_relative.description:
The largest standard deviation a value may carry: EDT, T20 and T30 relative, C50 and C80
in dB, D50 as a fraction, Ts in s, SPL in dB.

measured_on.description:
What the calibration was measured on beyond what the code checks (particles and crossings
per particle, in `calibration`): [`noise::calibration::MEASURED_ON`].

method.description: The run's computation method, which picks the calibration.

refused_resamples_allowed.description: Resamples that may refuse a quantity before its value is refused.

seed.description:
The bootstrap's seed, as `0x` and 16 hex digits: as a JSON number above 2⁵³ it would not
survive a reader that parses numbers as doubles.

uniform_lambert_max_mean_absorption.description:
Energetic T20 and T30: a band whose every face is Lambert with scattering 1 and has the
same absorption takes `uniform_lambert_walls` up to this mean absorption, and the other
bands' entry above it.

NoiseModel.description: What a series' noise is estimated from.

oneOf.description:
Receiver crossings, each adding `mean_deposit` on average, in the series' unit (with
several sources, the largest of theirs).

particles.description:
Particles per source (`nbparticules`), from which a refusal names the count that
would bring its value within its limit; `null` when not known.

run.description:
The run behind the series, for the calibration's correction and domain. `null` only
for a series that is no run's (a synthetic one in the tests): then `n` is taken as 0
and no domain is checked. Every model `core::results` makes from a run carries it.

oneOf.description: Nothing bounds the noise; every value is refused, `noise_unknown`.

NotEvaluable.description: Why a quantity cannot be read from a valid series.

oneOf.description: The decay, with the unseen tail added, never fell to the bottom of the range.

needed_db.description: The bottom of the evaluation range, dB (negative).

reached_db.description: How far the decay had fallen when the series ended, dB.

oneOf.description: The energy after the series' end could move the value by more than `limit`.

limit.description: The largest difference allowed, in the quantity's unit (relative for decay times).

value.description: The value from the series alone. Not reported as the quantity.

with_tail.description:
The value with the estimated tail added; `None` when the tail is unbounded (the
series was not decaying at its end), or when the decay curve with the tail spends too
little time in the range to fit.

oneOf.description:
The arrival was not given, and where in the onset bin it lies moves the value by more
than `limit`: `low` and `high` are the values with the arrival at the two ends of the bin.

limit.description:
The largest distance allowed from `value` to either end, in the quantity's unit
(relative for decay times).

value.description: Midway between `low` and `high`. Not reported as the quantity.

oneOf.description: The decay curve spends less time inside the range than a regression needs.
The fitted slope is not negative.
A window the quantity divides by holds no energy.

Energy is missing from the series: the solver dropped each particle once its energy fell to
`floor_db` below its start ([`EnergySeries::with_solver_floor`]), or lost particles
mid-path ([`EnergySeries::with_lost_share`]). With the most energy that can have cost
added, the decay is not shown to fall to the bottom of the range.

needed_db.description: The bottom of the evaluation range, dB.

reached_db.description: How far the decay had fallen, the unseen tail and the missing energy included, dB.

oneOf.description:
With the most energy the solver's floor or its lost particles can have cost added, the
value moves by more than `limit`.

value.description: The value from the series. Not reported as the quantity.

with_missing.description:
The value with the missing energy added; `None` when that curve cannot be fitted.
When the lost share follows the decay, the value moved by the most that share can
move it.

oneOf.description:
The series' early reverberation is not resolved
([`EnergySeries::with_early_reverberation_unresolved`]), and where it begins moves the
value by more than `limit`: `continued` is the value with the reverberation beginning at
the arrival (the decay of the first bin wholly after the direct sound continued back to
it), and `low` and `high` the lowest and highest over that and the reverberation beginning
at the start or at the end of that bin (`None` when one of those curves gives no value).

limit.description:
The largest distance allowed from `value` to either, in the quantity's unit (relative
for decay times).

value.description: Midway between `low` and `high`. Not reported as the quantity.

oneOf.description:
The value's Monte-Carlo standard deviation, estimated from the receiver crossings behind
each bin and calibrated against SPPS's own seed-to-seed spread ([`noise`]), is above
`limit`; or more than [`noise::REFUSED_RESAMPLES_ALLOWED`] of the resampled series refuse
the quantity themselves.

limit.description: In the quantity's unit (relative for decay times).

particle_count.description: The particle count that would bring the value within its limit, or why none is named.

sd.description:
Calibrated, in the quantity's unit. `None` when fewer than two resampled series give
a value.

value.description: The value from the series. Not reported as the quantity.

oneOf.description: The series' Monte-Carlo noise cannot be estimated, so nothing bounds it.

value.description: The value from the series. Not reported as the quantity.

oneOf.description:
The run lies outside what the noise model's calibration measured for this quantity
([`noise::calibration`]): fewer particles per source than its fewest, or more crossings of
a receiver per particle than its most. The model's standard deviation is not known to
bound the noise there, so the value is refused whatever it reads.

crossings_per_particle.description:
The run's crossings of the receiver per particle, as the calibration measures them
([`noise::calibration::variable`]).

max_crossings_per_particle.description: The most crossings per particle it measured this quantity at.

min_particles.description: The fewest particles per source the calibration measured this quantity at.

particles_at_least.description: When the run has too few particles: `min_particles`, the count to run at least.

receiver_radius_scale_at_most.description:
When the run has too many crossings per particle: the most the receiver radius may be,
as a multiple of the run's (crossings per particle grow as its square):
`√(max_crossings_per_particle / crossings_per_particle)`.

value.description: The value from the series. Not reported as the quantity.

oneOf.description:
More than one source contributes to the series. ISO 3382-1 defines the onset-relative
quantities per source–receiver pair, and a sum of several sources' responses is not one.
Made by `core::results`, which knows the sources; `params` never sees them.

The solver wrote no energy time series for the receiver, so there is nothing to compute the
quantity from. Made by `core::results` for TCR, whose receiver tables hold steady-state
levels only; `params` never sees such a receiver.

detail.description: The solver, and where its own values for the receiver are.

Onset.description: The onset bin: the first bin whose energy is within [`ONSET_THRESHOLD_DB`] of the largest.

ParamError.description: A refusal, with its code ([`ParamError::code`]) and what caused it.

oneOf.description:
The diffuse ray transport (`params::lambert`) cannot run with its inputs, a ray left the
enclosure, its mean free path is not `4V/S` within its statistical error, or `γ²`'s
standard error is above its limit.

Kuttruff's reference does not describe this band: not every face reflects by Lambert's
law with scattering 1 in it (`results::reference`); or no computed band has such walls, so
the transport was not run.

Parameters.description: The eight parameters of one band (or of the aggregate).

d50.description: A fraction, 0 to 1 (shown as a percentage).

ParticleCount.description: The particle count a refusal for Monte-Carlo noise names, or why it names none.

oneOf.description:
`factor` times the run's particles would bring the calibrated standard deviation to the
limit over `margin`, from its fall as `1/√N`: `(margin·sd/limit)²`
([`noise::calibration::margin`]). `particles` is that many per source, rounded up to two
significant digits, when the run's count is known.

More than [`noise::REFUSED_RESAMPLES_ALLOWED`] resamples refuse the value (rule R4-3):
`multiple` times the run's particles, the smallest of [`noise::RESAMPLED_MULTIPLES`] at which
the model's own resamples of the series, every deposit over `multiple`, refuse it at most
[`noise::RESAMPLED_REFUSALS_NAMED`] times and its calibrated standard deviation times
`margin` is within the limit. `particles` is that many per source, when the run's count is
known.

More than [`noise::REFUSED_RESAMPLES_ALLOWED`] resamples refuse the value, and they still
do, or its standard deviation is still above the limit, at `multiple` times the run's
particles, the largest tried (R4-3): no count is named, and more particles may not help.

More than [`noise::REFUSED_RESAMPLES_ALLOWED`] resamples refuse the value, and for this
quantity in this computation method the counts its resamples named were not borne out at
a higher count (round 4, F8): no count is named.

The fall of the seeds' spread as `1/√N` was not confirmed for this quantity in the run's
computation method ([`noise::calibration::root_n_confirmed`]), so no count is named.
Fewer than two resamples give a value: there is no standard deviation to scale.

ParticleFileSummary.description: A saved particle file (`nbparticules_rendu` > 0), decoded and summarised.

particles.description:
The particles written: those of the `nbparticules_rendu` per source that recorded at least
one step (`docs/formats/pbin.md`).

recorded_steps.description: Their step records, all particles together.

ParticleStats.description: The whole table: one entry per band column, in file order.

oneOf.description: C_te, `te` in seconds.
D_te, `te` in seconds.

QuantityCalibration.description:
How one quantity's noise is calibrated, where the calibration holds, and how a refusal names a
particle count (`params::noise::calibration::Entry`).

factor.description:
`k`: the largest one-sided 95 % upper bound, over the calibration cells, of the ratio of
the seeds' spread to `√(1 + kappa·n)` times the bootstrap, rounded up to two digits
(rule R3-1).

kappa.description: `κ`: how much a particle's crossings of one receiver at several times add (R3-1).

lambert_walls.description:
Energetic T20 and T30 only: the entry for bands whose every face reflects by Lambert's law
with scattering 1 and not every face has the same absorption (or the absorption is above
`uniform_lambert_max_mean_absorption`), the same as `entry` since round 4; `null`
otherwise.

margin.description:
A refusal names the particle count at which the calibrated standard deviation would be
the limit over this margin: one run's own estimate scatters from seed to seed, so a
count named from one run can fall short (rule 5b over round 3's calibration cells).

max_crossings_per_particle.description:
... and the most crossings per particle, `n`. Outside it the value is refused,
`noise_uncalibrated`.

min_particles.description: The domain (R3-5): the fewest particles per source the quantity was calibrated at ...

resampled_confirmed.description:
Whether a value its resamples refuse names the count at which they would not (R4-3):
false where such counts were not borne out at a pair's higher count (round 4, F8).

root_n_confirmed.description:
Whether a refusal names a count: the seeds' spread did not fall slower than `1/√N` on
any pair of cells that differ only in `N` (rule R3-6, one-sided).

structure.description: How the resamples the factor applies to are drawn ([`super::Structure`]).

uniform_lambert_walls.description:
Energetic T20 and T30 only: the entry for bands whose every face reflects by Lambert's law
with scattering 1 and has the same absorption, at most
`uniform_lambert_max_mean_absorption`; `null` otherwise.

ReceiverBandReport.description: One band of an SPPS point receiver.

arrival.description:
The arrival C50, C80, D50 and Ts are measured from: the direct sound at the receiver's
centre, `arrival_s`, spread over `±R/c` (`params::decay::Arrival::Known`), or `detected`.

complete.description:
SPPS's statistics show that at most one particle in a million was still alive when the
steps ran out (random mode, `trans_epsilon` above 0: `spps::SppsResults::band_complete`),
so the series is given to `params` as complete and no tail after its end is bounded.
Otherwise `params` bounds that tail. **Lost particles, and those few left alive, do not
make a band incomplete:** the energy their unfinished paths would have brought is bounded
separately, `lost_share`.

contributing_sources.description:
The sources whose energy reaches the receiver in this band (their `.recps` total is above
0). With more than one, the seven onset-relative parameters are refused,
`several_sources`.

crossings.description:
The receiver crossings behind the series, estimated as its total over the mean deposit;
`null` when the noise has no model.

crossings_per_particle.description:
`n`: the crossings of the receiver per particle as the noise calibration measures them
(`monte_carlo.crossings_variable`), which its correction and domain take
(`params::noise::NoiseModel::multi_crossing`); `null` when the noise has no model or the
series is refused.

curvature.description: T20 against T30: the curved-decay flag.

decay_curve.description:
The Schroeder curve EDT, T20 and T30 were fitted to, thinned for display
(`params::decay::DecayCurve`); `null` when the series is refused, or when several sources
contribute (the decay of their sum is no source–receiver pair's).

early_reverberation_unresolved.description:
Always true for SPPS, whose reverberation begins with the first reflection: how it ran
between the arrival and the first bin wholly after the direct sound is not known, so each
value is read three ways, with the reverberation beginning at the arrival (the decay of
that bin continued back), at that bin's start and at its end, is taken midway between the
lowest and highest of the three, and is refused, `early_unresolved`, when either lies
further than its limit from that midpoint
(`params::EnergySeries::with_early_reverberation_unresolved`). `decay_curve` shows the
first reading only.

energy_pa2.description: The `.recp` column, Pa² per time step.

floor_db.description:
The level below a particle's start at which SPPS drops it, dB, when that can cost the
histogram energy (energetic mode: `-10·trans_epsilon`); `params` bounds what it can have
dropped. `null` otherwise.

lost_follows_decay.description:
Energetic mode: what the lost particles would still have brought falls with the decay, so
`lost_share` bounds the energy from every time on, not a lump added at the end.

lost_share.description:
The share of the energy from the arrival on that unfinished particles (lost, or in a
complete band left alive at the end) can have taken with them
(`spps::SppsResults::lost_share`), or, when `lost_follows_decay`, that lost particles can
have taken of the energy from every time on (`spps::SppsResults::lost_share_following_
decay`); `params` bounds what it can move. `null` when there are none.

noise_model.description: What the values' Monte-Carlo noise is estimated from (`params::noise`).

onset.description: The first bin within 20 dB of the largest; `null` when the series is refused.

source_power_rho_c.description:
The sources' power in this band times `ρ·c` (the `.gap`), Pa²·m²: the free field's
mean-square pressure at distance `r` is this over `4πr²`.

air_m_per_metre.description:
The energy attenuation the solver applies, added as `4·m·V`, 1/m; `null` with air
absorption off.

eyring_s.description: Plain Eyring, `K·V/(4·m·V − S·ln(1 − ᾱ))`, s, with SPPS's `K`: **reported only**.

kuttruff_s.description:
Kuttruff's corrected Eyring, `K·V/(4·m·V + A_K)`, s, with `γ²` from the room's geometry:
**M8's reference**. `mc_sd` is only the standard deviation it inherits from the transport's
`γ²`, not its total uncertainty: it leaves out the formula's own error against a diffuse
room (−0.41 % to +0.59 % in M8's cells, `docs/params.md`, "Kuttruff's reference"; not
measured in other rooms). Refused with the transport's own refusal when the transport
refused, and `params_reference_not_applicable` where `lambert_walls` is false: it is
computed only where it describes the band.

lambert_walls.description:
Every face reflects by Lambert's law with scattering 1 in this band: the only walls the
transport's `γ²` describes. When false, neither time describes the run's field.

mean_absorption.description: `ᾱ = Σ Sᵢ·αᵢ / S` over the room's faces.

uniform_absorption.description: Every face has the same absorption in this band.

ReferenceReport.description: The analytic reference of an SPPS run, or why there is none (`results::reference`).

free_paths.description:
The diffuse transport's free paths in the room: the mean free path, `γ²`, their
standard errors, `4V/S`, and the transport's settings. `null` when the transport
refused, every band's `kuttruff_s` then carrying its refusal; and when no computed band
has Lambert walls, so that it was not run, every `kuttruff_s` then refused
`params_reference_not_applicable`.

RunNoise.description: What the calibration's correction and domain need from the run behind a series.

bands.description: The bands summed into the series: 1 for a band. Each band has its own particles.

lambert_walls.description:
Every face reflects by Lambert's law with scattering 1 in the band (in every band of an
aggregate); false when the run's reference was not computed.

least_deposit.description:
The smallest of the contributing sources' mean deposits: crossings per particle counted
at it are at least each source's own.

lifetime_cv2.description:
The spread of the particles' lifetimes, [`lifetime_cv2`] of the band's room table (the
largest over the bands of an aggregate).

mean_absorption.description: The faces' mean absorption in the band, `ᾱ` (the largest over an aggregate's bands).

receiver_crossing_s.description:
How long a particle takes to cross the receiver sphere, `2R/c`, s: the roughness
structure's blocks are at least this long ([`roughness_block`]).

uniform_absorption.description:
Every face has the same absorption in the band (in every band of an aggregate); false
when the run's reference was not computed.

SourceBandReport.description: One source's own echogram at a receiver, one band.

arrival.description: As for the receiver's band, from this source's own arrival.

energy_pa2.description: The source's `.recp` column, Pa² per time step.

SourcePoint.description: A source as SPPS reads it.

balloon.description:
`directivite` is 5, a directivity balloon: SPPS scales each particle's energy by the
balloon's value in its direction (`sppsNantes.cpp:115-127`), so its particles do not all
carry `W/N`.

band_power_w.description:
Its power in each computed band, W, as SPPS computes it: `10⁻¹²·10^(db/10)` in `f32`
from its `bfreq@db` children sorted by `freq` and taken by position
(`base_core_configuration.cpp:140-150`). Each of its particles starts with this over
`nbparticules` (`sppsNantes.cpp:73`).

emission_s.description:
When its particles start: `ceil(delay / dt)` steps, cast to `u16`
(`sppsNantes.cpp:91`), times `dt`.

position_m.description:
The position SPPS stores (`f32`); `None` when a coordinate is not one SPPS's reading is
emulated for (`run::locate::to_float`).

SourceReceiverReport.description:
One source's own echogram at a receiver (`output_recp_bysource`): the parameters of that
source–receiver pair, as ISO 3382-1 defines them.

arrival_s.description: The direct sound's arrival from this source, as for the receiver.

SourceTotals.description: One source's total at a receiver, per band (`.recps`).

arrival_s.description:
The direct sound's arrival at the receiver's centre, which every onset-relative parameter
is measured from (`params::decay::Arrival::Known`): the earliest over the sources;
`null` when it is not computed (a celerity gradient, or a position not read), and the
parameters then use `Arrival::Detected`.

by_source.description: Each source's total per band, Pa² (`.recps`), in `config.xml`'s order.

per_source.description:
Each source's own echogram and its parameters, when `output_recp_bysource` is on; empty
otherwise.

receiver_crossing_s.description: `2R/c`: the direct sound is spread over this long at a receiver.

reference.description:
The analytic reference on the run's own inputs (`results::reference`): Kuttruff's
corrected Eyring with `γ²` from the room's geometry, M8's reference, and plain Eyring,
reported only. **Not validated.**

total_energy.description: The energy in the room per band and step (`<cumul_filename>`).

Structure.description: How a series' resamples are drawn, per quantity ([`calibration::Entry::structure`]).

oneOf.description: M7's: every crossing deposits `d̄` on average, in every bin.

The run's own roughness (round 4): each bin's deposit read from how far the series' blocks
stray from their neighbours' geometric mean ([`roughness_deposits`]), at most `d̄`. In
energetic mode a particle's energy falls at every reflection, so late in a decay a
crossing deposits far less than `d̄`, by how much depending on how far the particles'
energies have spread apart, which SPPS does not write but the series' own roughness shows.

SurfaceReceiverSummary.description: One receiver of a surface file.

id.description:
`xmlIndex`: its id in `config.xml`, of a `recepteur_surfacique` in a receivers' file and of
a `recepteur_surfacique_coupe` in a cutting planes' file.

value_sum.description: The sum of every stored value.

SurfaceSummary.description:
One surface-receiver or cutting-plane file, summarised (the values stay in the file; M12 reads
it with the `.csbin` reader).

aggregate.description: [`AGGREGATE_GLOBAL_FILE`] for the `Global` file; `null` for a band's.

band_hz.description: The band; `null` for the `Global` file, **an aggregate of all bands**.

cutting_plane.description:
The cutting-plane file (`rs_cut.csbin`), not the surface receivers' (`Sound level.csbin`):
told apart by the file's name, and each holds exactly the receivers `config.xml` gives it.

TcrGlobal.description: TCR's `Global` row: the energetic sum of the band levels, **an aggregate**.

TcrReceiverBandReport.description:
One band of a TCR point receiver: TCR's own levels, dB, and the eight parameters, every one
refused `no_time_series`.

parameters.description:
TCR writes steady-state levels, not an energy time series, so `core::params` has nothing
to compute from: each of the eight is `params_not_evaluable`, `no_time_series`. Its SPL
too, because TCR gives two totals, Sabine's and Eyring's, and neither is `params`' SPL of a
series; they are `total_sabine_db` and `total_eyring_db`.

TcrReceiverGlobal.description:
A TCR receiver's `Global` row: each column's energetic sum over the bands, **an aggregate**
(`ctr/input_output/reportmanager.cpp:131-143`).

TcrReceiverReport.description:
A TCR point receiver, in the same shape as an SPPS one where the two meet: `label`, `bands[]`
with `freq_hz`, `parameters`, `curvature` and `decay_curve`, and `aggregate`.

aggregate.description:
SPPS's shape, labelled [`AGGREGATE_NO_SERIES`]: no band summed, every parameter refused
`no_time_series`.

label.description: The file's name without `.gabe`: exactly one `recepteur_ponctuel@lbl`.

TcrReport.description:
A TCR run: its values as TCR computed them, and `core::params`' analytic Sabine and Eyring
times on the same inputs. TCR writes no time series, so every per-receiver parameter is
refused, `no_time_series`.

Theory.description: One theory's values in one band of `Main results.gabe`.

Variable.description: What `n`, the multi-crossing variable, is (rule R3-2, per method).

oneOf.description:
The crossings of the receiver per particle, `n1`
([`super::crossings_per_particle`]).

`n1` times the spread of the particles' lifetimes, `Var L/(E L)²`
([`super::lifetime_cv2`]): a particle alive late has more crossings ahead of it when
the decay has a long second slope.

status.description: Always OK: any other run is refused.

validated_by_bed.description: False until M8's physics bed passes: no number here may be shown to a user.
